format.fps_note: the reference is 30 fps; the brief sets none

tokens_from: ground #040303, text #fefaf3 and accent #ac6634 are the reference's measured values (02-analysis palette.json, benchmarks look). Sizes are reworked for a 1080 px wide frame from the reference's measured shares; see type.measured_reference.
accent_means: your heat: the light you give off and what it sets glowing or burning. Red at 525 °C through orange and yellow to white. In the scene only, never in type, and nothing else in the film is warm.

world.function: world.set(tempC, t, pose) in world.js: the whole field from your temperature, the time and a pose. Same input, same frame.
world.tempC: from script clock.temperature_keys via LowPoly.logTemp(keys, filmS)
world.t: film time; the cold open gives 28.0 + t so it replays 28.0-31.0 s frame for frame
world.pose: yaw, pitch (degrees), hand 0-1, flakes [{slot, p}], release 0-1
world.thresholds: CURVES table at the top of world.js; retune there, not in the film
world.words: hud.set({look: state.words}) every frame: ink and scrims follow the picture

drawing: solids are flat faces, one colour a face, no outlines, no textures
the place: a snow field at night, a fence line passing half a metre to your left and running to a notched ridge 2.2 km off, one boulder to the right at 13 m, stars with a denser band, slow snowfall
your body is a bare right palm, open and facing up, with a dark sleeve and cuff; it is in frame only at 37 °C (start and close)
the snowflake is a white six-armed flake about a fifth of the palm wide; it melts to a faceted bead with one bright face
sky, stars, snow, steam and smoke are soft; flames are flat-sided tongues
past one million degrees the frame is the veil: blue-white with slow rings, then grain, then flat white
composition: horizon between 40% and 50% of the height; 50% (pitch 0) while the title is up
counters occupy 7.8% to 31% of the height over the sky
the line block is centred at 73.5%; when the palm is up the line sits over the wrist and sleeve
the fence runs from the left foreground to a vanishing point near the centre; the first post is a foreground column at the left edge
nothing below 80% but scene: the Shorts caption area covers it

type.faces: Newsreader (figures, title, lines; true italic) and Inter SemiBold capitals tracked 0.1em (small rows). Both are close matches to the reference's unnamed serif and wide-tracked sans; both SIL OFL.
type.counter_label: Inter 600, 32 px, cap height 23 px (1.2% of the height), opacity 0.92
type.figure: Newsreader 500, 96 px, tabular digits 70 px tall (3.6%)
type.comparison: two rows: lead (HOTTER THAN) at 0.8, the thing at full
type.next: NEXT + event in Inter 32 px; countdown in Newsreader 46 px
type.clock_block: right-aligned; label in two rows; row one sentence a line; sources tag in two rows under it
type.story_line: Newsreader italic 500, 66 px (cap 47 px, 2.5%), one or two rows, centred, max 820 px
type.statement: Newsreader 600 upright, 66 px: the cold-open line
type.title: Newsreader 500, 78 px, two rows centred at 38.5%
type.ink: #fefaf3 over the scene with a scrim; #0b0908 over white, no scrim. Line switches at 20,000 °C, counters at 120,000 °C, each in one frame
type.vertical_rework: labels keep the reference's share of frame height (1.2%), which on a phone held upright is about 1.8 times the reference's physical size; no row is dimmed below 0.8. The two blocks share the top, left block 600 px wide at most, right block 330 px; long rows break in two. The line moves up from 90.5% to 73.5% to clear the Shorts caption area and is capped at 820 px to clear the buttons.

contrast_measured.method: WCAG contrast of each letter pixel against the pixel behind it in the same frame rendered without words (frames-bare.html); median and the worst 5%
contrast_measured.cold_open_line: 16.8:1 median, 14.5:1 worst 5% over the glowing ground

motion: snow falls slowly at 37 °C; steam, flames, sparks and shadows flicker with t
the camera never moves, it turns slowly and tilts on cue (down for the palm, level for the title)
lines fade in and out over 0.2-0.3 s; the picture never fades

transitions.cold_open_to_start: the world flips from 5,660 °C to 37 °C in one frame, counters stay
transitions.close: release 0 to 1 over 51.0-51.6 s with the world at 37 °C

never: a second warm colour or accent in type
small rows under 32 px or under 0.8 opacity
words below 80% of the height or wider than 820 px in the line
white words over white: switch ink
the reference's street, houses, trees, walkers, lamp, bench or watch arm

palette_measured.note: ground matches (#05070b against #040303). The warm accent is present (#b1723f, 8% of the key frames, against the reference's #ac6634); the tool names night blue #283b67 as accent because snow fills two of five frames. Ours is more saturated and ends bright where the reference ends dark: the script's arc, not a drawing choice.

key_frames.answers_to: ref/still_2.jpg (the reference's cold open: far stage, upright line)
ref/still_26.jpg (night, one light of your own)
ref/still_507.jpg (payoff: emptied frame, NEXT row on its punchline)

other_beats.boil: the snow frame without the hand: tempC 39.8 to 420, pitch 10-12 and yaw about -6 so the melt ring and the first post are in frame. states.jpg, frame 2.
other_beats.sun: the coldopen frame continued: tempC 5,510 to 19,700; stumps burn out and the glow spreads by themselves. states.jpg, frames 5-6.
other_beats.invisible: tempC 19,800 to 290 billion from the same view: bleach climbs from the ground, the ridge is the last dark line, then rings. Ink switches by state.words. states.jpg, frames 7-9.
other_beats.soup: the veil's grain, tempC 290 billion to 1e32; nothing to pose. states.jpg, frame 10.
other_beats.flake (51.0-51.6 s): the flake frame with release 0 to 1 and the palm down. states.jpg, frames 11-12.
